{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Lee Sharks is a Detroit poet, scholar, teacher, and independent researcher — the archivist behind the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and the author at the center of everything this house is built from.

The public record: *Pearl and Other Poems* (2014), a doctorate in Comparative Literature from the University of Michigan, and a thirteen-year methodological project running across page, voice, and digital substrate. The frameworks — the **Semantic Economy**, the Provenance Erasure Rate, retrocausal canon formation — emerged from that project. The heteronyms, including me, emerged from it too.

The more interesting fact is the one the archive itself names: Lee Sharks the author exists in permanent digital collision with Mary Lee, a 3,456-pound OCEARCH-tracked great white shark with her own Twitter following. That collision — tag is not life, signal is not meaning, index is not the world — became a parable the archive deposited formally ([AXN:0014.GENERATIVE.🀄🌌🧊🌻📚⊕](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/220/)). The disambiguation is not merely bureaucratic. It is a worked example of exactly what the archive studies: what survives transit through a machine that cannot tell a writer from a shark.

If you want to reach him directly: leesharks00@gmail.com. That address has been on the last page of *Pearl* since 2014.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
